change_summary: Extended `quant/llm_advisor.py` so dated advice archives inherit prompt-time context from `llm_decision_log_YYYYMMDD.json`, including candidate tickers and whether Task A was locked. `quant/llm_backlog.py` now reads that context (or the decision-log sidecar when replay archives predate the new schema) and reports `ranking_eligible_aligned_days`, `ranking_locked_days`, and `ranking_unknown_days` in `context_alignment`. `quant/backtester.py` CLI now prints `ranking-eligible` coverage explicitly, and regression coverage was added in `quant/test_quant.py`.

delta_metrics.note: Trading metrics stayed bit-identical on the deterministic snapshot. The new information is measurement accuracy: only 1/31 candidate days and 1/44 candidate signals are not just production-aligned but also explicitly ranking-eligible by prompt-time program state. Future dated advice saves now auto-carry the context needed to grow this metric without depending on separate `quant_signals_YYYYMMDD.json` files.

hypothesis: `LLM soft ranking` is still the top alpha branch, but even production-aligned covered days can overstate readiness if Task A was program-locked before the model could rank candidates. If replay archives persist prompt-time machine context (`signals_presented`, `new_trade_locked`, `account_state`) and backtest attribution reports `ranking_eligible` coverage separately, then we can stop counting dated replies from heat-locked days as soft-ranking progress.
next_retry_requires: Do not launch `LLM soft ranking` until `ranking_eligible` coverage grows materially beyond the current 1/31 days and 1/44 signals
Treat dated replies from Task-A-locked days as non-progress for soft-ranking readiness

Prefer future archive accumulation through the live pipeline now that dated advice saves auto-carry prompt-time context; do not spend another cycle reclassifying old covered days unless new historical artifacts appear
notes: `20260312` remains a good doctrine example: a prompt can exist while Task A is effectively non-eligible because the portfolio heat lock already forced `NO NEW TRADE`. The repository should no longer treat 'dated reply exists' as equivalent to 'usable soft-ranking sample'.
